promoted: {rival}, your batchmate and your rival for every promotion, is promoted to {title}. The email announcing it is copied to you too, as a courtesy.
{rival}, your batchmate, is now {title}. The group chat from your first year hears about it before you do.
{rival}, your batchmate, makes {title}. {They} sent round a very nice message, which you have read twice.
winService: This year there was one promotion slot at your grade, and two of you up for it: you and {rival}, your batchmate and your rival for every promotion. It went to you. {rival} congratulated you within the minute, so the news must have reached {them} first.
The ranking exercise could promote only one of you at this grade, and it was you. {rival}, your batchmate, took it well, in the sense that nobody saw {them} take it.
loseService: This year there was one promotion slot at your grade, and two of you up for it: you and {rival}, your batchmate and your rival for every promotion. It went to {rival}. You're told it was "very close". That is what everyone is told, probably including {rival}.
The ranking exercise could promote only one of you at this grade, and it was {rival}, your batchmate. {senior}, your reporting officer, says you are "next in line", and doesn't say for what.
winPolitics: There was one appointment open at your level this year, and the choice was between you and {rival}, your batchmate. It went to you. {rival} was the first to shake your hand at the swearing-in, and held it a beat longer than necessary.
losePolitics: There was one appointment open at your level this year, and the choice was between you and {rival}, your batchmate. It went to {rival}. The Prime Minister's Office describes the decision as "finely balanced".
pm: {rival}, your batchmate, is to be the next Prime Minister. {They} telephoned you before the announcement, or said {they} did.
pmBlocked: The one job above yours is taken. {rival}, your batchmate, is Prime Minister, and shows no sign of having considered the private sector.
The one job above yours is still taken. {rival}, your batchmate, has announced a ten-year plan, which you are choosing to read as a policy document.
elected: {rival}, your batchmate, was introduced at a press conference as a new candidate for Parliament, and won, and is now a Member of Parliament.
lostSeat: {rival}, your batchmate, ran for Parliament and lost the ward. A month later {rival} was back in the service at the same grade, which everyone agreed to call a homecoming.
consultancy: {rival}, your batchmate, is leaving the service for the private sector. The farewell lunch is at a hotel, so the new package must be very good.
scandal: {rival}, your batchmate, has resigned, for personal reasons. Everyone has a theory. Nobody says it in the lift.
rankedBelowService: The ranking exercise put {rival}, your batchmate and your rival for every promotion, above you this year. Neither of you went up: the slot went to someone from another division whom you have never met.
You were ranked just below {rival}, your batchmate, this year, and neither of you was promoted. It is the one comparison everyone on the floor made, and nobody made out loud.
rankedBelowPolitics: When the appointments were settled, the name of {rival}, your batchmate, was ahead of yours on the list. Neither of you moved. Someone with no government job at all did.
appointed: {rival}, your batchmate, is appointed {title}. The swearing-in photograph is on the front page, and you are in the background of it.
{rival}, your batchmate, is now {title}. The group chat from your first year hears about it before you do.
promotedApart: {rival}, your batchmate, is now {title}. You hear about it at a dinner, from someone who assumes you already knew.
{rival}, your batchmate, is now {title}. The group chat from your first year hears about it before you do.
electedTogether: {rival}, your batchmate, stood at the same general election, in another constituency, and won, and is now a Member of Parliament too.
lostSeatTogether: {rival}, your batchmate, stood at the same general election, in another constituency, and lost. A month later {rival} was back in the service at the same grade, which everyone agreed to call a homecoming.
consultancyPolitics: {rival}, your batchmate, has left Parliament for a seat on a company's board. The papers call it "an orderly transition". They call all of them that.
scandalPolitics: {rival}, your batchmate, has resigned from Parliament, for personal reasons. Everyone has a theory. Nobody says it in the lobby.
retired: {rival}, your batchmate, retires as {title}. At the farewell lunch, {rival}'s speech thanks "my batchmate, {player}". You send a card afterwards, and mean it.

folder.item: a peer assessment of {rival} that did you more good than it did {them}

events.title: The 360
events.body: It's 360-degree feedback season, when colleagues assess each other anonymously and the ranking panel reads the results. You've been asked to assess {rival}, your batchmate and your rival for every promotion. The form promises anonymity. It has a free-text box headed "Areas for development".

choices.outcome: Three sentences on stakeholder management, true and mildly painful. {rival} acts on all three within a year and never learns where they came from.
It is accurate. It is also the only peer comment the ranking panel quotes. {rival} is described that year as "still developing", which you did not write but did cause.
The form accepts it. HR's report later notes "limited peer input" for your whole division. Your blank form is one of the reasons.

events.title: Annex B
events.body: {rival}, your batchmate and your rival for every promotion, sends a paper up to the Permanent Secretary at nine tomorrow, and you're copied on the draft. Annex B has the right numbers in the wrong columns, and the recommendation rests on them. A mistake like that would cost {rival} at the next ranking.

choices.outcome: {rival} fixes it at 11:50pm and says thank you twice, the second time in a voice you have not heard before.

choices.text: Say nothing. It is not your paper.
choices.outcome: The Permanent Secretary finds Annex B in four minutes. For the rest of the year {rival} is described as "detail-light". You are described as nothing at all, which this year is better.

choices.text: Raise it at the meeting, helpfully.
choices.outcome: You are thanked for your rigour. {rival} thanks you too, later, in the corridor, in a tone the minutes would not have captured.

events.title: One Posting
events.body: There's one two-year posting to the Budget Division at the Ministry of Finance this year, the kind that gets people noticed, and your division has two nominees: you and {rival}, your batchmate. HR suggests the two of you "have a conversation" first. In HR, that means one of you should withdraw.

choices.text: Withdraw, and say it was your idea.
choices.outcome: {rival} goes to Finance. Three weeks later a photograph arrives of the view from {their} new office. It is, admittedly, a very good view.

choices.text: Let HR decide on the files.

contest.winText: The posting goes to you. {rival} says {they} had expected it to, which may even be true.
contest.loseText: The posting goes to {rival}. HR's email to you uses the phrase "many strong candidates". There were two.

choices.outcome: HR decides on the files, which takes six weeks and a matrix.

choices.text: Make your case to the Director, privately.

contest.winText: The posting goes to you. {rival} hears, eventually, how.
contest.loseText: The posting goes to {rival}. The Director mentions, in passing, that {rival} did not come asking.

choices.outcome: The Director listens, nods, and promises to "bear it in mind". That is the most anyone has ever got out of that office.

events.title: Views Are Sought
events.body: {rival}, your batchmate, has been shortlisted for a post one grade above you both, which would make {rival} senior to you. The selection panel has asked {rival}'s peers for their views. Yours will be read, and filed, and remembered by someone.

choices.outcome: You write half a page and mean all of it. Someone on the panel later shows it to {rival}, who never mentions it to you and never forgets it.
Two lines, both true, neither memorable. The panel files them with the others.

choices.text: Suggest, carefully, that another year in the grade might help {them}.
choices.outcome: The panel finds your view "balanced". {rival} learns of it eventually, the way everyone here learns everything: from someone who was not supposed to say.

events.title: Saturday
events.body: {rival}, your batchmate, is an MP too, and {rival}'s ward has had a difficult year: a lift upgrading that overran, and an angry letter in the newspaper every week. {They} asked you to walk the ward with {them} on Saturday morning. Your own ward has a walkabout planned for the same morning.

choices.outcome: Six blocks, two markets, and one auntie who assumes you are {rival}'s campaign manager and tells you exactly what she thinks of {them}. The letters to the newspaper stop by March. The last one thanks "the MP from the next ward, {player.formal}".
Your volunteers are better at it than you are. {rival} thanks them by name, which you notice.
Your ward is pleased to see you. {rival} manages without you, and remembers the Saturday.

events.title: First Among Equals
events.body: Who becomes the next Prime Minister, first among equals, is being settled informally by the Cabinet, in a room. It has come down to two names, as the officers you joined with joked it would at your first dinner together: {player} and {rival}.

choices.outcome: You say it plainly, to the people who need to hear it. {rival} says it too, in the next room. It will be decided the way these things are: slowly, and then all at once.
{rival} thanks you once, in private, and never again. That is how you know the deal was understood.

events.title: The Name Put Forward
events.body: {rival}, your batchmate and now senior to you, has been asked to nominate officers for a cross-ministry task force. Everyone understands it is where future leaders get tested. {They} put your name first.

choices.outcome: Lunch, on you, at a place {rival} chose. It was more expensive than {they} let on, and worth it.

choices.text: Decline. You would rather go up on your own file.
choices.outcome: {rival} says that is fair. It is, and it costs you a year.
